- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment periods.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30d horizon, especially after recent spikes; add 1–2% to early forecast values.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +2% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment (≤0.3) in last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if recent 5-day average is >70, forecast tends to dip below; if <65, tends to rise — adjust toward 68–72 range if sentiment is neutral.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true price by 2–4 days; if sentiment is rising, anticipate 1–2 day lead; if falling, expect 1–2 day lag.
